speaker: Unknown
en: Hey folks, my name is Sydney.
zh: 大家好，我叫 Sydney。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm the product manager for the open source team at LangChain.
zh: 我是 LangChain 开源团队的产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today I'm super excited to share with you how you can build a model router in the harness to reduce cost without sacrificing quality.
zh: 今天我非常激动地和大家分享，如何在 harness 中构建一个模型路由器，在不牺牲质量的前提下降低成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's jump in.
zh: 让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the motivating problem for building a model router is that frontier intelligence is really expensive.
zh: 那么，构建模型路由器的动因问题是，前沿智能真的非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're building agents that work at scale, this cost can be prohibitive.
zh: 如果你正在构建大规模运行的智能体，这个成本可能会高得令人望而却步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so model routing can help to reduce cost theoretically without sacrificing quality if it's done well.
zh: 而模型路由如果做得好，理论上可以在不牺牲质量的前提下帮助降低成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a quote here showing that model providers like Anthropic even recommend starting with smaller models, in this case like Claude Haiku, before graduating to a more intelligent model like Opus because a lot of tasks can be done with these cheaper models.
zh: 我这里引用了一段话，显示像 Anthropic 这样的模型提供商甚至推荐先从小模型开始，比如 Claude Haiku，再升级到像 Opus 这样更智能的模型，因为很多任务用这些更便宜的模型就能完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm basically assuming here that we often don't need the best model for a lot of tasks that we ask our agent to do.
zh: 所以我在这里基本上是在假设：对于很多我们让智能体去做的任务，我们往往不需要最好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Past a certain point, you kind of hit diminishing returns where your cost and latency are increasing, but the quality of the outputs are not significantly better.
zh: 超过某个点之后，你会有点陷入收益递减：成本和延迟在增加，但输出的质量并没有显著变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ideally, an agent has good model harness task fit.
zh: 理想情况下，智能体应该有良好的模型-harness-任务契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: It means you have the right model for the job on the intelligence and cost curve here, and then your harness does a good job of getting the right context to the model for the given task at hand.
zh: 意味着你在智能和成本曲线上为工作选择了正确的模型，而且你的 harness 能很好地把当前给定任务所需的正确上下文传给模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does a model router actually do?
zh: 那么模型路由器到底是做什么的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It picks the right model for each task.
zh: 它为每个任务挑选正确的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a task request comes in and a router has a classifier model and then a prompt with some criteria that help it decide what model would be most appropriate for a given task.
zh: 一个任务请求进来，路由器有一个分类器模型，然后配合一个带有某些标准的提示词，帮助它决定哪个模型最适合给定的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So would that be a fast and cheap model, maybe something balanced or a performance focused model that's going to be slower and more expensive?
zh: 那么，那会是一个快速且便宜的模型，或许是某种均衡的模型，还是一个专注于性能、会更慢更贵的模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it selects the given model for the task.
zh: 然后它为该任务选出给定的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then that model is used to power the agent that completes the task.
zh: 接着用那个模型来驱动完成任务的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our testbed here was OpenSui, our open source coding agent.
zh: 我们的测试平台是 OpenSui，我们的开源编码智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to kind of spoil the results of the experiment here, we were able to see a 64% reduction in median cost per thread with no measurable change in quality.
zh: 提前剧透一下实验结果：我们实现了每线程中位成本降低 64%，且质量没有可测量的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's four steps for building a model router and I'll explain them through the lens of this OpenSui experiment that we ran.
zh: 构建模型路由器有四个步骤，我会通过我们进行的这个 OpenSui 实验的视角来讲解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a little sneak peek here.
zh: 不过先稍微剧透一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, you need to understand the tasks that your agent works on.
zh: 第一步，你需要了解你的智能体处理的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to understand the models available for these tasks.
zh: 你需要了解这些任务可用的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then with one and two done, you can build the router in your agent's harness.
zh: 然后在完成第一和第二步之后，你可以在智能体的 harness 中构建路由器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very important to track task outcomes so that you can understand if your router is working well.
zh: 并且，跟踪任务结果非常重要，这样你才能了解你的路由器是否运行良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is reducing cost without sacrificing quality.
zh: 也就是说，在不牺牲质量的前提下降低成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so let's talk about step one, understanding the tasks.
zh: 好，我们来谈谈第一步，了解任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing that we did was try to understand what our coding agent OpenSwe is being tasked with.
zh: 我们做的第一件事，就是试图了解我们的编码智能体 OpenSwe 被分配了什么任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was all done using LangSmith.
zh: 这全部是使用 LangSmith 完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So every time our coding agent runs, it sends a trace to LangSmith that has a record of every step that that agent took.
zh: 所以每次我们的编码智能体运行时，它都会向 LangSmith 发送一条 trace，记录该智能体所采取的每一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were able to use all of those traces and do aggregate analysis over them to determine what types of tasks our agent was doing.
zh: 于是我们能够利用所有这些 trace 并对它们做聚合分析，来确定我们的智能体在执行什么类型的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can see here, unsurprisingly for a coding agent, that code changes dominated things like feature requests, bug fixes, and tests.
zh: 你可以在这里看到，对于一个编码智能体来说毫不意外，代码变更占据了主导，比如功能请求、bug 修复和测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there were also some things like design questions and general purpose questions.
zh: 但也有一些像设计问题和一般性问题这样的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of all of the steps, I would actually say that this one is the most important.
zh: 在所有步骤中，我其实要说过一步是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what you use as the foundation for building your criteria for the router.
zh: 这是你构建路由器标准时所用的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, deciding what types of tasks should be assigned which model.
zh: 就是决定什么类型的任务应该分配哪个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you don't have a clear understanding of this task space, it's going to be very hard to develop an effective router.
zh: 所以如果你对这个任务空间没有清晰的理解，就很难开发出一个有效的路由器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And LangSmith, as I mentioned, was very instrumental for us in helping understand this space.
zh: 而 LangSmith，正如我提到的，对我们理解这个任务空间非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually built a custom app on top of LangSmith to help me better understand this trace data.
zh: 我实际上在 LangSmith 之上构建了一个自定义应用，来帮助我更好地理解这些 trace 数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can see kind of the categories here and then active agent time and observe LLM cost filtered by different types of requests.
zh: 你可以在这里看到类别，然后是智能体活跃时间和 LLM 成本，按不同类型的请求过滤。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overall, this was super helpful for basically exploratory data analysis over my traces.
zh: 总的来说，这对我对 trace 做探索性数据分析非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also as part of step one, I wanted to better understand how complexity varied by task type, knowing that we probably want a more intelligent model for more complex tasks.
zh: 作为第一步的一部分，我还想更好地了解复杂度如何随任务类型变化，因为我们知道对于更复杂的任务，我们可能需要更智能的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can see here, we measured median invocations, so that's the number of times OpenSwee was called, and then also the median LLM cost for these different buckets of tasks.
zh: 你可以在这里看到，我们测量了中位调用次数，也就是 OpenSwee 被调用的次数，还有这些不同任务类别的中位 LLM 成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we generally rated a task as more complex if the number of invocations were higher or the LLM cost was higher.
zh: 我们一般把调用次数更多或 LLM 成本更高的任务评为更复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see kind of unsurprisingly here that like feature work was generally more complex than say testing work.
zh: 你可以在这里看到，毫不意外，功能工作通常比测试工作更复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, so this part is actually quite fun.
zh: 好，这部分其实相当有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Step two is understanding the models available for your tasks.
zh: 第二步是了解你的任务可用的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this data is pulled from the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index as of September 9th, 2026, which is when we began this experiment.
zh: 这些数据来自截至 2026 年 9 月 9 日的 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index，也就是我们开始这个实验的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see on the x-axis, we have the cost per intelligence task.
zh: 你可以看到在 x 轴上，是每个智能任务的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on the y-axis, we have the artificial analysis intelligence index.
zh: 然后在 y 轴上，是 artificial analysis 智能指数。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what we call the Pareto frontier for LLMs.
zh: 这就是我们所说的 LLM 的帕累托前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a set of optimal models that have a good trade-off between benchmark accuracy and evals compared to cost and latency.
zh: 它是一组最优模型，在基准准确率和评测与成本和延迟之间有很好的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so generally we want to select models along this frontier.
zh: 所以一般来说，我们想沿着这条前沿选择模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then given that we were designing a model router, we wanted to choose a small set of models here that had some trade-offs between their speed and intelligence index.
zh: 然后鉴于我们在设计一个模型路由器，我们想在这里选一小组模型，它们在速度和智能指数之间有一些权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models that we ended up choosing were GLM 5.3 Flash for our fast model, GPT 5.6 Sol for our balanced model, and then GPT 6 Astra for our performance tier.
zh: 我们最终选择的模型是 GLM 5.3 Flash 作为我们的快速模型，GPT 5.6 Sol 作为我们的均衡模型，然后 GPT 6 Astra 作为我们的性能档。

speaker: Unknown
en: Step three is building the router in the harness.
zh: 第三步是在 harness 中构建路由器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we used two sources of data to decide on the criteria for our initial version of the router.
zh: 我们使用了两个数据来源来确定路由器初始版本的判断标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first was the understanding of those tasks that we saw in step one.
zh: 第一个是我们在第一步中看到的对这些任务的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second was the official provider guides from OpenAI, for example, on which models to use for which tasks.
zh: 第二个是来自 OpenAI 等供应商的官方指南，关于哪些任务该用哪些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can see a couple of the descriptors that we used for each of the criteria for a given model.
zh: 你可以看到我们为给定模型的每条判断标准所使用的一些描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also important to note for our router here, the router just runs once on the thread's first message and then selects the model for the remainder of the task.
zh: 这里对我们的路由器同样重要的是，路由器只在该会话线程的第一条消息上运行一次，然后为任务的其余部分选定模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is different from some routers which do this like mid-flight routing.
zh: 这与一些做类似中途路由的路由器不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: We decided to just do a simple version for our first pass, but when I talk about upcoming improvements or further work, mid-thread routing is covered.
zh: 我们决定第一版只做一个简单的版本，但当我谈到即将到来的改进或后续工作时，会讲到线程中途路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we initially built this router in early September, we used a small LLM, specifically GLM 5.3 Flash, to do the routing decision with structured output.
zh: 所以当我们在 9 月初最初构建这个路由器时，我们使用了一个小型 LLM，具体是 GLM 5.3 Flash，通过结构化输出来做路由决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: But after the experiment, JEV, a popular decision model, came out and had claims of being significantly faster and cheaper than LLMs with more constrained decision-making powers.
zh: 但在实验之后，JEV，一个流行的决策模型，发布了，声称比 LLM 明显更快更便宜，且决策能力更受限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we are now powering our OpenSWE router with JEV, the decision model,
zh: 所以我们现在用 JEV 这个决策模型来驱动我们的 OpenSWE 路由器，

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's much faster and much cheaper, as Jeb advertised.
zh: 而且它确实如 Jeb 宣传的那样，快得多也便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last thing I'll call out on this slide is that GLM 5.3 Flash is actually an open model.
zh: 我在这页幻灯片上要指出的最后一件事是，GLM 5.3 Flash 实际上是一个开源模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: At LangChain a while ago, we wrote a blog about open models crossing a threshold.
zh: 在 LangChain 之前，我们写过一篇关于开源模型跨越门槛的博客。

speaker: Unknown
en: We definitely think that's true.
zh: 我们确实认为那是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use open models a lot internally, and a model router is a great opportunity to experiment with using cheaper and faster open models for tasks that they're more than equipped to handle.
zh: 我们内部大量使用开源模型，而模型路由器是一个很好的机会，可以试验用更便宜更快的开源模型来处理它们完全能胜任的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, and then for step four, you need to decide how you're going to track your task outcomes.
zh: 好的，然后第四步，你需要决定如何追踪你的任务结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two main ways you can do this.
zh: 主要有两种方式可以做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is through offline evals.
zh: 第一种是通过离线评测。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is very safe.
zh: 这非常安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have, you know, repeatable comparisons and experiments that you can run.
zh: 你可以运行可重复的比较和实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the catch is that it can be a little bit hard and expensive to develop a representative dataset.
zh: 但问题在于，开发一个有代表性的数据集可能有点困难且昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the faster approach here is to do an A-B test where you know that your live traffic is representative.
zh: 所以这里更快的方法是做 A-B 测试，这样你就知道你的线上流量是有代表性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the catch here is that, you know, we're running this experiment for our live users.
zh: 但问题在于，我们是在为线上用户运行这个实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they may experience a non-optimal router, which is the risk.
zh: 所以他们可能会体验到非最优的路由器，这就是风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the two outcomes that we were tracking with our AB test were the merged PR rate.
zh: 我们在 AB 测试中追踪的两个结果是 PR 合并率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also we enabled users to provide feedback on OpenSwee runs so they could either give a thumbs up or a thumb down.
zh: 另外我们还让用户可以对 OpenSwee 运行提供反馈，他们可以点赞或点踩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can imagine we want to make sure that for the 50% of threads that run through this new router, the merged PR rate doesn't go down significantly and the feedback is not significantly different either.
zh: 你可以想象，我们想确保对于通过这个新路由器运行的 50% 会话线程，PR 合并率不会显著下降，反馈也没有显著差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, so experiment number one, what were our results?
zh: 好了，那么实验一，我们的结果是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We had almost 500 threads, and you can see that the median cost per thread for the router was much lower, 64% lower.
zh: 我们有将近 500 个会话线程，你可以看到路由器的每线程中位成本要低得多，低了 64%。

speaker: Unknown
en: The mean cost was also lower, and then the P90 cost per thread was lower by 37%.
zh: 平均成本也更低，然后每线程 P90 成本低了 37%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see actually for this case more threads from the routed version ending in a merged PR, although the difference was not statistically significant.
zh: 在这个案例中，我们实际上看到路由版本有更多会话线程以 PR 合并结束，尽管差异在统计上不显著。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also see that the PR open rate was pretty comparable across our A and B branches.
zh: 然后我们还看到 PR 打开率在我们的 A 和 B 分支之间相当接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see on this breakdown kind of the proportion of tasks that were sent to each of the model tiers.
zh: 你可以在这个细分中看到发送到每个模型档的任务比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had 34% sent to the fast tier, 56% sent to the balanced tier, and only 10% sent to performance.
zh: 我们有 34% 发送到快速档，56% 发送到均衡档，只有 10% 发送到性能档。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see on the far left kind of the different distribution of costs for the
zh: 你可以在最左边看到成本的不同分布，对于

speaker: Unknown
en: Always performance model versus the routed.
zh: 总是性能模型对比路由版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can see on the right side for the routed threads, we had much cheaper fast runs and then the performance runs.
zh: 然后你可以在右边看到，对于路由的会话线程，我们有便宜得多的快速运行，然后是性能运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on the right, you can see in aggregate, the fast runs were much cheaper and then balanced and performance more expensive accordingly.
zh: 然后在右边，你可以看到总体上，快速运行便宜得多，然后均衡和性能相应地更贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: One interesting note, we definitely did see a couple of very long threads contributing disproportionately to cost.
zh: 一个有趣的点，我们确实看到几个非常长的会话线程不成比例地推高了成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was true for both the routed and non-routed arms of the experiment.
zh: 这在实验的路由和非路由两个分支中都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will note, we actually started a second experiment, which was router versus a controlled fast model.
zh: 我要说明的是，我们实际上启动了第二个实验，即路由器对比受控的快速模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the first experiment, it was a control of the performance model.
zh: 所以在第一个实验中，对照是性能模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did end this test within a day because we got so many complaints from users who were stuck on the fast arm.
zh: 我们确实在一天之内结束了这次测试，因为我们收到了很多用户投诉，他们被卡在了快速那条臂上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we got enough complaints.
zh: 所以我们收到了足够多的投诉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't want to significantly degrade user experience.
zh: 我们不想显著降低用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we decided to stop this experiment.
zh: 于是我们决定停止这个实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was pretty telling.
zh: 但这已经很说明问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We certainly couldn't switch over to GLM 5.3 Flash for all of the tasks that OpenSuite needs to manage.
zh: 我们当然无法把 OpenSuite 需要管理的所有任务都切换到 GLM 5.3 Flash 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's next here?
zh: 那么接下来该做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's definitely a lot that we could do to further explore model routing optimizations.
zh: 肯定还有很多可以做的，来进一步探索模型路由的优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first thing would be benchmarking the router on other eval sets like DeepSuite rather than just doing the A-B testing.
zh: 我认为第一件事是在其他评测集上对路由器做基准测试，比如 DeepSuite，而不只是做 A-B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or even perhaps other benchmarks that are more review focused because generally the task for OpenSuite is to generate good reviewable PRs.
zh: 或者甚至也许是其他更侧重于 review 的基准，因为总的来说 OpenSuite 的任务是生成好的、可 review 的 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing that we didn't touch is model selection for sub-agents.
zh: 第二件我们没碰的事情是子智能体的模型选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's definitely more cost optimizations to be made if we also select appropriately sized models for the sub-agents that the main agent orchestrates with the deep agents harness.
zh: 所以肯定还有更多成本优化空间可做，如果我们也为子智能体选择大小合适的模型——这些子智能体是主智能体通过 deep agents harness 来编排的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A third thing that I mentioned earlier we could certainly explore is rerouting mid-thread.
zh: 第三件事，我之前提到过，我们当然可以探索的是对话中途重新路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can imagine if for OpenSwee, a user asks a question and then discovers that maybe a pretty complex bug fix is in order or wants to design a new feature mid-thread, you might want to upgrade to a more capable model.
zh: 你可以想象，对于 OpenSwee，用户先问了一个问题，然后发现可能需要一个相当复杂的 bug 修复，或者想在对话中途设计一个新功能，这时你可能想升级到更强能力的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And rerouting mid-thread could help to ensure that the right model is chosen for the task at any point in the given thread.
zh: 而对话中途重新路由可以帮忙确保在任何给定的对话节点上，都为手头任务选择了正确的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: One trade-off here is that if you do switch a model, you experience a cache miss, which can be costly.
zh: 这里有一个权衡：如果你切换了模型，你会遇到一次缓存未命中，这可能是昂贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for async agents like OpenSuite, there's actually a lot of cache misses anyways, just because there's more than a five minute idle time between when an agent responds and a developer has time to respond back in Slack.
zh: 但对于像 OpenSuite 这样的异步智能体来说，其实本来就有很多缓存未命中，只是因为从智能体响应到开发者有时间在 Slack 里回复之间，有超过五分钟的空闲时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this cache miss might actually not be a super significant concern.
zh: 所以这个缓存未命中实际上可能不是一个非常值得担心的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the fourth thing would be digging for richer routing signals.
zh: 然后第四件事是挖掘更丰富的路由信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we didn't get a ton of feedback on traces.
zh: 我们并没有从 traces 上得到太多反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did get, you know, the PR merge rate was a very reliable metric, but trying to get more active feedback would be helpful as well.
zh: 我们确实得到了，你知道的，PR 合并率是一个非常可靠的指标，但尝试获取更多主动反馈也会很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to get started building your own router, I would recommend following the four steps that we did in this experiment.
zh: 所以如果你想开始构建自己的路由器，我建议按照我们在这个实验中做的四个步骤来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one, understand your agent's task space.
zh: 一，理解你的智能体的任务空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, pick models along the Pareto frontier, the cost intelligence curve.
zh: 二，沿着帕累托前沿、也就是成本-智能曲线来挑选模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Third, treat routing as context engineering and build your router into the harness where the appropriate context is for the given tasks at hand.
zh: 第三，把路由当作上下文工程来对待，把你的路由器构建进 harness 里，也就是对于眼前的给定任务、合适的上下文所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fourth, make sure you have the power to measure success before you begin live routing.
zh: 第四，在开始线上路由之前，确保你有能力衡量成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can easily add routing to your own agent with our model routing middleware.
zh: 你可以用我们的模型路由中间件，轻松地为你的智能体添加路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at LinkChain, we've always prided ourselves on offering open source software that's model provider agnostic.
zh: 而在 LinkChain，我们一直以提供模型提供方无关的开源软件而自豪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so changing models in your router should just be a one line of code change.
zh: 所以在你的路由器里更换模型，应该只需要改一行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also check out OpenSwee at LinkChainAI slash OpenSwee on GitHub.
zh: 你也可以在 GitHub 上的 LinkChainAI slash OpenSwee 查看 OpenSwee。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can learn more about building a harness with GEV, which is a decision model that's incredibly powerful for the model routing step, at the blog linked below.
zh: 你可以在下方链接的博客中，了解更多关于用 GEV 构建 harness 的内容，GEV 是一个决策模型，对于模型路由这一步来说非常强大。

en: And we always love hearing from you.
zh: 而且我们总是很乐意听到你们的声音。

speaker: Unknown
en: Feel free to tag us at linkchain on X.
zh: 欢迎在 X 上 @我们 linkchain。
